primitives.name: Bond Yield Shock Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Regime: mixed with a risk-off tilt — orderly rotation, not breakdown.** The 10-year tagged 5.35%, its highest since 2002, before a strong $22B 30-year auction (5.618%, 2.54x bid-to-cover) pulled it back to 5.231%, and Brent ripped past $105 after Trump rejected an Iran deal.
primitives.assumptions: Yield curve inversion implies recessionary expectations; oil spike increases inflation premium.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Rate-driven equity sell-off with broadening risk-off sentiment.

layer2.mapping: Yield curve steepness maps to equity sector rotation via risk premium dynamics; oil price acts as exogenous shock variable.
layer2.telemetry: 10Y yield level, oil price trajectory, QQQ drawdown

primitives.name: Equity Rotation Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: This is the market repricing the multiple in the bond pit while rotating underneath — painful for cap-weighted tech, survivable for everything else.
primitives.assumptions: Market allocates capital from high-multiple growth to value sectors; tech underperforms due to valuation compression.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Cap-weighted tech decoupling from broader market dynamics.

layer2.mapping: Rotation index derived from relative performance of growth vs. value ETFs; captures structural shift in portfolio allocation.
layer2.telemetry: QQQ vs. IWM, SPY vs. energy/staples ETFs

primitives.name: Risk-Off Tolerance Threshold
primitives.verbatim_quote: TLT's +0.95% bounce confirms the bond bid arrived once yields stopped rising; VIX at 15.57 says hedging, not fear; gold flat says no real safe-haven scramble.
primitives.assumptions: Bond demand surge indicates risk-off behavior without panic; VIX reflects hedging rather than fear.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Orderly risk-off with controlled volatility and no flight-to-safety.

layer2.mapping: VIX and TLT return form a dual measure of risk-off sentiment; gold flatness indicates no systemic flight-to-quality.
layer2.telemetry: VIX level, TLT bounce, gold price stability

The bond yield shock operator models how 10Y and 30Y yields respond to oil price spikes, creating a feedback loop that pressures long-duration tech equities. The rotation index tracks this shift through sectoral performance differentials, particularly between QQQ and IWM. Risk-off tolerance evaluates whether this rotation is orderly or panic-driven by monitoring VIX and TLT behavior. These primitives form a triadic system where yield dynamics drive rotation, which is then modulated by risk appetite. The failure mode occurs when oil shocks exceed threshold yield levels, triggering broad-based equity sell-offs beyond sectoral rotation.
